unit.why: A short anecdote, quoted from the Hida's Shem ha-Gedolim, about the Maharshal (a pre-Hasidic rabbinic authority) who ordered a rebuker to come daily and admonish him while he listened in awe.
unit.boundary_note: part of a chain of exempla on keeping a rebuker (previous: Avodat ha-Gershuni; next: an unnamed tsaddik from Pe'er Kedoshim)

stories.summary_en: While serving as rabbi and head of the court, the Maharshal ordered a preacher to come every day for an hour and rebuke him like a commoner, and he would wrap himself and listen in awe and trembling.

tags.why: praise of the Maharshal, a pre-Hasidic authority, copied from the Hida's Shem ha-Gedolim
set in a chain of exempla teaching that one should accept rebuke and keep a rebuker

quotes: צוה למוכיח אחד שיבוא בכל יום
tags.why: the hired rebuker (mokhiah) is a distinct character

quotes: ויוכיחנו ויזהירנו כאלו הוא א׳ מהמון
tags.why: a chief rabbi asks to be rebuked like a commoner

quotes: לשמוע תוכחות מוסר ביראה ורעדה לפני ה׳
tags.why: he listens to the rebuke in awe
trembling appears in a stock phrase
he wraps himself (in his tallit) before the rebuke
